title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) to measure the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the declared/requested model gpt-5-mini we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, audit-grounded reconciliation of provider-call accounting, an artifact-grounded explanation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and prescriptive boundary conditions where guarded stages are likely to matter.

sections.introduction:
Recent proposals to use generative large language models (LLMs) for NetOps emphasize intent→configuration translation and automated change workflows. Operational safety requires generated artifacts to satisfy syntactic, ordering, and higher-order policy constraints; practice commonly layers deterministic validators with optional sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures. Prior survey and systems reports document these generate→validate→repair patterns and motivate workflow-centred evaluation, but they lack large-scale paired measurements isolating the marginal value of sandboxed emulation when the same generated candidate is analyzed by both conditions [1]–[3].

Research question and contributions. We asked: under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution on Npairs = 720; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis reporting exact counts, tests, and CIs; (3) a concise provider-call audit reconciliation that explains asymmetric audit counters arising from shared-initial-generation semantics and limited repair activity; (4) an evidence-grounded interpretation clarifying boundary conditions where guarded stages add operational value.
sections.related_work:
The literature has converged on two practical themes relevant to our design. First, surveys and architectural reports document the prevalence of LLM-assisted NetOps and advocate layered defenses—deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops—to raise assurance for intent→configuration pipelines [1], [2]. Second, tool-focused case studies show that static configuration analyzers have matured rule-sets but still miss some runtime-dependent behaviors; emulation or symbolic execution can surface such gaps in prototype settings [2], [3].

Synthesis and gap. Collectively, prior work motivates pairing generation with verification and execution-harnesses but does not provide preregistered paired estimates that isolate the downstream marginal contribution of sandboxed emulation under controlled generation semantics. Our study fills that narrow experimental gap by enforcing shared_initial_candidate semantics so that any between-condition discordance can only arise downstream of generation (emulation observations or repair).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We preregistered a paired confirmatory protocol (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) with primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, target Npairs = 720, and a preregistered minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20. Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds; missingness and contamination plans were fixed before execution.

Task bank and topology abstractions. Confirmatory items were generated deterministically from the intent_configuration_repair_v1 family and cover three abstract vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, explicit intent, required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break).

Modeling and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses); the client-specified max_output_tokens = 2000 and did not set an explicit temperature parameter. Per the preregistration, for each pair a single sampled initial candidate was obtained and the same candidate was fed to both downstream conditions (baseline and guarded). This isolates any paired discordance to downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation observations or permitted repair calls).

Baseline validator. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 applies deterministic, rule-based checks: vendor-CLI parsing and canonicalization; sequence-order checks against required_command_sequence; atomicity and group-level workflow constraints; protected-interface invariants; and final-state conformance. It emits a binary detection flag and a validator_trace containing parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, and violation detail codes.

Guarded pipeline and sandboxed emulation. The guarded pipeline runs the baseline validator and then executes the candidate in an automated sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the topology and executes normalized CLI commands on vendor-abstracted virtual devices. The harness records runtime observations (interface transitions, transient concurrent states, MTU/VLAN application effects, and topology-level reachability) and applies a conservative mapping of those observations to detection flags when runtime semantics reveal violations not encoded in the static validator.

Repair policy. The preregistered policy allowed at most one repair-stage model invocation per task, callable only after initial generation and downstream observations for the guarded condition. All repair calls and transcripts were recorded.

Provider-call audit and reconciliation (required revision addressed). The execution manifest and reconciliation artifacts record provider-call auditing fields: hosted_model_call_event_count (total model calls), stage_counts (per-stage call counts such as shared_initial_generation and repair), and condition_counts (labels attached to specific stage events). In our run hosted_model_call_event_count = 721 with stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. The apparent asymmetry in condition_counts (keys labeled "shared":720 and "guarded":1 in the audit) arises from the shared_initial_candidate protocol: the shared_initial_generation stage produced a single candidate per pair (720 calls) that was consumed by both downstream conditions, and the single repair-stage call (1) occurred only in the guarded pipeline. Thus the audit fields count model-call events by lifecycle stage, not per-condition independent generations; under shared_initial semantics a single shared_initial_generation maps to both conditions while a repair-stage call maps only to the guarded condition. Deterministic_reconciliation and provider-call audit artifacts reconcile these counts with episode accounting and show no provider-call failures.

Analysis plan. The preregistered primary analysis used a paired-binary executor (McNemar-style inference with exact two-sided test) and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). Secondary per-class and per-vendor paired analyses were pre-specified as exploratory with multiplicity adjustments. The primary analysis excluded no paired episodes (complete_pair_count = 720).
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and statistics (artifact-grounded). Contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. These figures are taken verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts.

Provider-call accounting and discordant-pair attribution. Provider-call audit records model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. Deterministic reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 720 and the contingency counts above. The single n10 discordant pair co-occurs with the single recorded repair-stage call; the archived raw_results record for that pair links baseline_score = 0, guarded_score = 1, and contains validator_trace plus repair_provider_trace entries. In the archived bundle that episode’s traces attribute the guarded-only detection to the single documented repair-stage invocation rather than to a guarded-emulation-only observation. The reconciliation artifacts and raw per-episode traces permit auditors to locate that pair by pair_id and inspect the exact validator and repair transcripts.
sections.discussion:
Why the guarded-stage marginal benefit was negligible. The artifact-grounded evidence indicates three primary factors:
(1) Validator ceiling effect and task-rule alignment. The deterministic validator encoded the same workflow patterns present in the curated task bank (e.g., shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break_uplink_switchover); most shared_initial candidates complied with validator rules (validator_trace violation_count = 0 for the vast majority), leaving little headroom for emulation to add detections.
(2) Curated, parser-validated task set. Inclusion required parser acceptance and deterministic generation, which reduced the prevalence of adversarial or malformed candidates that emulation would otherwise uncover.
(3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and minimal repair activity. By design all pairs used the same sampled candidate; only a single repair-stage call occurred across the run, and the single guarded-only detection maps to that recorded repair activity in the archived traces.

Operational implications. In operator regimes that enforce strong prevalidation and employ high-coverage static validators aligned to expected intents, automated sandboxed emulation may deliver minimal incremental detection benefit. Guarded sandboxing remains valuable when inputs are noisier or adversarial, vendor diversity is broader, or emulation fidelity can reveal long-lived control-plane semantics.

Scope and auditability. The run’s archived artifacts provide an auditable chain from aggregated counts to the single discordant episode and the recorded repair-stage call. Because the study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20, observing ≈0.0014 indicates a narrow near-zero effect for the tested regime rather than a general negative result about guarded stages in all settings.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator to the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a vanishing aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call auditing shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair), and reconciliation links the unique guarded-only detection to the single documented repair-stage invocation. We conclude that, in tightly curated and parser-validated task regimes where validators are closely aligned to expected workflow patterns, a guarded sandbox adds negligible marginal detection coverage. Follow-up work should retest guarded stages on adversarial, uncurated, multi‑vendor, or higher‑fidelity-emulation task banks; the archived bundle provides concrete seed traces and per-episode records to support such extensions. For independent audit, the canonical execution manifest and per-episode raw_results are archived as part of the run’s reproducibility bundle (see Disclosure).

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: Autonomous post-lock research run executed under the frozen master prompt supplied to the system. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration id: f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e (preregistration was created and frozen before confirmatory execution). Initial master-prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Run accounting summary (artifact-grounded): completed_episode_count = 1440, complete_pair_count = 720, model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared-initial generation calls + 1 repair-stage call); stage_counts and provider-call audit are archived in the execution manifest and reconciliation artifacts. Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad NetOps topic family and constrained the pre-lock master prompt; after the autonomy lock the agentic pipeline autonomously performed literature selection, preregistration, code and prompt generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, and manuscript drafting. No manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock. The canonical execution manifest and per-episode artifacts referenced above serve as the authoritative reproducibility bundle for this study.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and long-lived control-plane interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.
